title: CobaltWorks POC quality + load scoping kickoff
summary: Kickoff to define acceptance criteria and benchmarking plan for a 6-week POC. Discussed golden prompt set, regression cadence, hallucination detection heuristics, load profile targets, initial benchmark timing, and security checkpoints (SOC2/KMS). Next steps: share benchmark template, sample prompt set, schedule baseline perf run, provide security pack.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. we're on for about an hour. i'm Maya from Redwood, AE on this account. quick intros?
[00:10] Jane Ortiz: Hey all, Jane, product. we own the customer-facing summarization flow.
[00:15] Mark Tennant: Mark, eng manager, i'll own the integration and load testing.
[00:20] Ravi Singh: Ravi, security. i'll be the point for compliance questions.
[00:25] Leo Park: Leo from Redwood SE, i'll run the benchmarks and set up the golden-set validations.
[00:30] Evan Lopez: Evan, ML eng, i'll help with sample data and metrics.
[00:35] Maya Chen: Great. goal for today is to lock down POC success criteria, what the golden prompts look like, regression cadence, and a rough load and timing plan.
[00:48] Jane Ortiz: High level, success metric is correctness on the summarization task and substantially fewer hallucinations than our baseline. we also need to ensure 95th perc latency under 700ms for typical short docs.
[00:58] Mark Tennant: For load, initial target is 50 qps sustained during peak sim, with bursts to 120 qps. we can throttle clients but want to see how batching behaves.
[01:10] Leo Park: Ok that's helpful. for correctness do you have a scoring rubric today? are you using ROUGE/EM or human labels?
[01:18] Jane Ortiz: It's a mix. offline we do BLEU/ROUGE but product cares about user-rated helpfulness. so we need a human-eval golden set plus automated heuristics.
[01:28] Leo Park: Perfect. for the POC we typically do a multi-prong eval: (1) a golden-set of ~200 examples for exact/regression checks, (2) a larger sample of 2k examples for statistical scoring, (3) hallucination heuristics and format validation, and (4) quality gates tied to human eval thresholds.
[01:42] Maya Chen: Timeline idea: 6 weeks total. Week 0-1 onboarding + baseline data ingestion, week 2 baseline perf and correctness, week 3 first golden run and small-scale load test, week 4 model/quant config tuning, week 5 full load benchmark and regression, week 6 acceptance review and write-up. does that align with your expectations?
[01:59] Mark Tennant: Yes that works. we can provide 2k anonymized transcripts by Friday.
[02:04] Evan Lopez: we'll scrub PII and give you a column format.
[02:08] Ravi Singh: security: we need to validate data residency and KMS key management. also SOC2 docs.
[02:15] Ana Ruiz: we'll send our security whitepaper and the SOC2 report after this call.
[02:20] Jane Ortiz: On quality side, hallucinations are the killer. can you describe hallucination checks you use?
[02:27] Leo Park: Sure. we combine lexical checks (named-entity mismatch heuristics), fact-checking via retrieval-based grounding where possible, and hallucination scoring that penalizes unsupported factual claims. we also check format constraints — e.g., if the summary must be <140 chars or include specific fields, that's validated. note some entity names are tricky in transcription — the K-V cache sometimes shows up as K-V cash in our transcripts, so tooling tolerates small mismatch.
[02:51] Jane Ortiz: Makes sense. for scoring, what's typical?
[02:54] Leo Park: We produce a composite score: 40% human helpfulness (sampled human labels), 25% automated factuality/hallucination score, 20% format/constraint pass rate, 15% latency/availability penalty. Each has thresholds; for acceptance we'd expect composite >= 0.78 and hallucination rate under 3% on the golden set.
[03:14] Mark Tennant: That hallucination target seems tight but reasonable. what's the false positive rate of your heuristics?
[03:19] Leo Park: Good question — on our internal datasets we see ~6-8% false positive detections on edge cases; hence we always pair heuristics with human review on flagged items.
[03:30] Maya Chen: On load, Leo, how will you simulate the batching patterns?
[03:34] Leo Park: We'll use a synthetic driver that mirrors your histogram of sequence lengths. if you can share typical doc length distribution (p95 tokens), we'll match it. batching rules: we test at batch sizes [1, 8, 32] and measure latency tail and throughput. we will also validate our prefix/KV cache warmup strategies for repeated user sessions.
[03:52] Evan Lopez: Our p95 doc is about 600 tokens, median 220. bursts happen around business hours 10-12.
[03:58] Leo Park: perfect — that informs kernel selection. note on quantization: if you want lower cost we can recommend int8/4 quant profiles but that may slightly increase hallucination unless we calibrate prompts.
[04:11] Jane Ortiz: Do you support private deployment? some of our PII flows will require VPC or private inference.
[04:16] Maya Chen: Yes — Redwood Private is an option. for the POC we can run hosted with strict retention controls, or if you need VPC we can arrange a dedicated sandbox. security team will coordinate.
[04:26] Ravi Singh: We'll need an architecture diagram and data flow, plus proof of encryption-at-rest and KMS integration.
[04:33] Ana Ruiz: i'll attach the architecture and a checklist in the follow-up email.
[04:38] Mark Tennant: about evaluation cadence: how often should we run regression tests?
[04:42] Leo Park: For POC: weekly runs against the golden set and nightly lightweight checks against a smaller random sample. if we detect regressions above a slack threshold (e.g., composite drop > 5 points), we triage and roll back to prior model variant.
[04:56] Jane Ortiz: who owns the golden set labeling? we can do in-house but limited bandwidth.
[05:00] Maya Chen: options: Redwood can help bootstrap labeling for the golden 200 examples, or we can provide crowd labels. many customers use Redwood to seed the gold set and then run a small in-house validation holdout.
[05:10] Jane Ortiz: ok may be easiest to have Redwood seed and we validate.
[05:14] Leo Park: We'll prepare a disposition file that shows each golden prompt, expected ground truth, and scoring rubric (pass/fail and partial credit notes).
[05:23] Mark Tennant: For benchmarking infra, do you need us to open firewall rules or provide load agents?
[05:28] Leo Park: We'll need an egress endpoint if hosted, and for dedicated sandbox we'll request a temporary VPC peering or IP allowlist. we'll share specifics in the benchmark template.
[05:36] Jane Ortiz: timeline check — when is first baseline perf?
[05:39] Maya Chen: We recommend baseline perf in week 2 so we can tune in week 3. so target baseline run on 2026-07-08.
[05:47] Evan Lopez: sounds good, we'll target dataset delivery by 2026-06-26.
[05:51] Ravi Singh: action on security: will review SOC2 and produce checklist by 2026-07-02.
[05:58] Leo Park: on artifacts we'll deliver: benchmark harness, golden-set template, hallucination heuristics doc, scoring rubric, and a short runbook for reproducing results.
[06:08] Jane Ortiz: any concerns about cost during POC?
[06:11] Maya Chen: we can provide a capped spend for hosted runs and show cost per 1k tokens for each config. if you prefer predictable cost, Dedicated reserve options exist but usually not needed for a POC.
[06:22] Mark Tennant: ok sgtm.
[06:24] Maya Chen: quick recap and next steps — i'll summarize.
[06:28] Maya Chen: Next steps: Maya to send benchmark template + pricing cap by EOD 2026-06-24; Leo to schedule baseline perf slot 2026-07-08 and prepare golden-set seed; Ana to send SOC2 + security whitepaper; Mark/Evan to deliver scrubbed dataset by 2026-06-26; Ravi to produce security checklist by 2026-07-02.
[06:50] Jane Ortiz: thanks everyone.
[06:53] Maya Chen: thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the baseline run. bye.
